messages:
Maya: Heads up — after the kernel 6.5.8 rollout in eu-west-1 we're seeing a spike in NCCL timeouts and intermittent Xid 13 on a subset of nodes (mixed A100p + A10x). Feels like a kernel/driver ABI mismatch or a NIC MTU regression.
Alex: Confirmed. Alert fired ~15:12 UTC: `nccl_timeouts_high` across two racks. p95 latency for all-reduce ops jumped 3x.
infra-bot: ALERT: `nccl_timeouts_high` eu-west-1 (rack-7, rack-9) — 12 nodes affected — triggered at 2026-03-18T15:12:08Z.
Sam: Logs show repeated `NCCL WARN` + `watchdog` messages and kernel oops with `xid 13` on some kernels. Kernel stackframes reference `nvidia_modeset` and `gdrdrv`.
Maya: Quick check — did we change MTU on the new kernel images? I remember a patch that defaulted to 9000 -> 1500 in cloud-init.
Troy: No, MTU left as-is in the kernel package. But the node bootstrap script applies interface tunings; I saw a change in the cloud-config that touches bonding. Rolling diffs now.
Alex: Repro steps from node: `kubectl exec -n infra -it gpu-debug -- ip link show` shows MTU 1500 on affected nodes, while healthy ones are 9000.
Sam: That explains NCCL reducing ring performance — fragmentation/segmentation causes transfer retries and triggers NCCL watchdog timeouts.
Maya: Can we hotpatch MTU back to 9000 on a single rack to confirm?
Troy: Doing a quick test on rack-7: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000` and restarting nvidia-persistenced on one node.
Alex: After MTU set and `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced`, I see NCCL latency drop and no immediate Xid 13. Prometheus `nccl_allreduce_p95` dropped back in 2 mins.
ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK SUGGESTION: If kernel upgrade introduces MTU changes, revert MTU OR revert kernel package. Steps: 1) quarantine affected nodes 2) set MTU 9000 3) restart nvidia services 4) monitor 30m 5) roll back kernel if not stable.
Maya: Good. Two parallel actions: (A) patch cloud-config to preserve MTU and reimage nodes; (B) hold kernel 6.5.8 for remaining pools. Which team takes A and B?
Sam: I'll own A (cloud-config). I'll prepare a small canary: rack-7 only.
Troy: I'll own B — pause the kernel auto-rollout in eu-west-1 and add a pin in the image registry to previous kernel 6.4.21 for GPU fleets.
Alex: Also recommending alert refinements: split `nccl_timeouts_high` by MTU and `xid_code` tag. Add a temporary runbook link to the alert. PromQL example to add:
```
avg_over_time(nccl_allreduce_duration_seconds[5m]) by (node) > 0.5
```
and a second filter: `label_replace(node_xid_count, "xid", "$1", "error_msg", "(xid \d+)")` (pseudo)
Maya: Can we add a synthetic check to the CI that runs a tiny NCCL allreduce on each kernel image before rollout? If it fails we block.
Sam: Yep — I'll add a smoke test in image pipeline: `cuda-sanity` job that runs `nccl_test` across two local containers (uses loopback). Fails fast.
Troy: Ops note: vendor driver stays at 535.86.02 — the kernel module recompile might be different with 6.5.x and `gdrdrv` needs the correct headers. We should also capture `dkms` build logs when packaging.
Alex: Filed a quick ticket: INFRA-2134 to add dkms build log archiving to S3; will attach to rollback postmortem.
Maya: Action items summary: Sam = cloud-config patch+canary; Troy = pause rollout + pin kernel; Alex = alert split + dkms logs; Sam & Troy = revert steps if canary fails.
infra-bot: NOTE: cluster autoscaler paused for eu-west-1 (safety) by Troy at 2026-03-18T15:34:10Z.
Sam: Canary results in rack-7 look good after 45m. No Xid 13, NCCL p95 stable. Rolling cloud-config patch to rack-9 next.
Troy: We'll keep kernel hold until full fleet validated. I'll publish a short blurb for SRE and oncall channels.
Maya: Runbook updates: add MTU checks and kernel-driver ABI matrix. I'll update the runbook with the exact `ip link` check and the prometheus query.
Alex: Closing note — strange edge case: nodes that had GPU firmware updated earlier had fewer failures. Firmware + driver + kernel interplay likely matters. Add GPU firmware version to node labels and to the export metrics.
Maya: Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open until eu-west-1 fully green. :thumbsup:
